They dominate him utterly; they are sufficiently baleful to transform him from an angel to a demon. He sees things through false light, and justifies himself for the commission of any monstrous act.

arxiv-1712-05284.title: Adaptation to criticality through organizational invariance in embodied agents
arxiv-1712-05284.creator: Miguel Aguilera, Manuel G. Bedia
arxiv-1712-05284.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Miguel Aguilera, Manuel G. Bedia. Many biological and cognitive systems do not operate deep within one or other regime of activity. Instead, they are poised at critical points located at phase transitions in their parameter space. The pervasiveness of criticality suggests that there may be general principles inducing this behaviour, yet there is no well-founded theory for understanding how criticality is generated at a wide span of levels and contexts.

arxiv-2109-07159.title: Note on the bundle geometry of field space, variational connections, the dressing field method, & presymplectic structures of gauge theories over bounded regions
arxiv-2109-07159.creator: J. François, N. Parrini, N. Boulanger
arxiv-2109-07159.description: Abstract In this note, we consider how the bundle geometry of field space interplays with the covariant phase space methods so as to allow to write results of some generality on the presymplectic structure of invariant gauge theories coupled to matter.

arxiv-2112-01096.title: Multistrange Hyperon Production on Nuclear Targets
arxiv-2112-01096.description: Abstract We consider the experimental data on yields of protons, strange Λ ′ \Lambda^{\prime} s, and multistrange baryons ( Ξ \Xi , Ω \Omega ), and antibaryons production on nuclear targets, and the experimental ratios of multistrange to strange antibaryon production, at the energy region from SPS up to LHC, and compare them to the results of the Quark-Gluon String

arxiv-2301-08189.title: Benchmarking YOLOv5 and YOLOv7 models with DeepSORT for droplet tracking applications Preprint: Version 1
arxiv-2301-08189.creator: Mihir Durve, Sibilla Orsini, Adriano Tiribocchi, Andrea Montessori, Jean-Michel Tucny, Marco Lauricella, Andrea Camposeo, Dario Pisignano, Sauro Succi
arxiv-2301-08189.description: Abstract Tracking droplets in microfluidics is a challenging task. The difficulty arises in choosing a tool to analyze general microfluidic videos to infer physical quantities. The state-of-the-art object detector algorithm You Only Look Once (YOLO) and the object tracking algorithm Simple Online and Realtime Tracking with a Deep Association Metric (DeepSORT) are customizable for droplet identification and tracking.

arxiv-2308-00434.title: Monotonicity of Equilibria in Nonatomic Congestion Games Journal: arXiv
arxiv-2308-00434.creator: Roberto Cominetti, Valerio Dose, Marco Scarsini
arxiv-2308-00434.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Roberto Cominetti, Valerio Dose, Marco Scarsini. This paper studies the monotonicity of equilibrium costs and equilibrium loads in nonatomic congestion games, in response to variations of the demands. The main goal is to identify conditions under which a paradoxical non-monotone behavior can be excluded. In contrast with routing games with a single commodity, where the network topology is the sole determinant factor for monotonicity, for general congestion games with multiple commodities the structure of the strategy sets plays a crucial role.

arxiv-2312-17336.title: PINN surrogate of Li-ion battery models for parameter inference. Part II: Regularization and application of the pseudo-2D model Journal: TBD
arxiv-2312-17336.creator: Malik Hassanaly, Peter J. Weddle, Ryan N. King, Subhayan De, Alireza Doostan, Corey R. Randall, Eric J. Dufek, Andrew M. Colclasure, Kandler Smith
arxiv-2312-17336.description: Abstract Bayesian parameter inference is useful to improve Li-ion battery diagnostics and can help formulate battery aging models. However, it is computationally intensive and cannot be easily repeated for multiple cycles, multiple operating conditions, or multiple replicate cells. To reduce the computational cost of Bayesian calibration, numerical solvers for physics-based models can be replaced with faster surrogates.

arxiv-2406-16296.title: Likelihood-based inference, identifiability and prediction using count data from lattice-based random walk models
arxiv-2406-16296.creator: Yihan Liu, David J. Warne, Matthew J. Simpson
arxiv-2406-16296.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yihan Liu, David J. Warne, Matthew J. Simpson. In vitro cell biology experiments are routinely used to characterize cell migration properties under various experimental conditions. These experiments can be interpreted using lattice-based random walk models to provide insight into underlying biological mechanisms, and continuum limit partial differential equation (PDE) descriptions of the stochastic models can be used to efficiently explore model properties instead of relying on repeated stochastic simulations.

arxiv-2407-02704.title: Monads, Comonads, and Transducers
arxiv-2407-02704.creator: Rafał Stefański
arxiv-2407-02704.description: Abstract This paper proposes a definition of recognizable transducers over monads and comonads , which bridges two important ongoing efforts in the current research on regularity. The first effort is the study of regular transductions, which extends the notion of regularity from languages into word-to-word functions.

arxiv-2510-07049.title: Dispersion and the transport of exciton-polaritons in an optical conveyor belt
arxiv-2510-07049.creator: Xingran Xu, Chunyu Jia, Xin-Xin Yang
arxiv-2510-07049.description: Abstract The growing interest in exciton-polaritons has driven the need to manipulate their motion and engineer their band structures to the forefront of contemporary research. This study explores the band structures that emerge from a spatially modulated potential, ingeniously realized through the use of an optical conveyor belt.

arxiv-2601-01510.title: Reduced-Rank Autoregressive Model for High-Dimensional Multivariate Network Time Series
arxiv-2601-01510.creator: Qi Lyu, Xiaoyu Zhang, Guodong Li, Di Wang † \dagger Shanghai Jiao Tong University, ‡ \ddagger Tongji University, § \lx@sectionsign University of Hong Kong
arxiv-2601-01510.description: Abstract Multivariate network time series are ubiquitous in modern systems, yet existing network autoregressive models typically treat nodes as scalar processes, ignoring cross-variable spillovers. To capture these complex interactions without the curse of dimensionality, we propose the Reduced-Rank Network Autoregressive (RRNAR) model.

pmc-11340583.title: Theater as a means of communicating research on climate change: The case of “Cambiare il clima”
pmc-11340583.creator: Elisa Vanin, Costantino Manes, Alvise Mattozzi, Lara Giordana, Micol Rispoli, Marco Andorno, Sebastiano Amadio
pmc-11340583.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Between 2018 and 2023, the Department of Environmental, Land and Infrastructure Engineering (DIATI) at the Polytechnic University of Turin (PoliTo) implemented a project to advance research and education on climate change monitoring, adaptation and mitigation solutions. As part of their communication efforts, DIATI partnered with Faber Teater to create the play “Cambiare il clima” (in Italian, this means “Change the Climate”).This involved a collaboration between DIATI researchers, communication officers, and Faber Teater.

pmc-11393455.title: Intrinsic dipole Hall effect in twisted MoTe2: magnetoelectricity and contact-free signatures of topological transitions
pmc-11393455.creator: Feng-Ren Fan, Cong Xiao, Wang Yao
pmc-11393455.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). We discover an intrinsic dipole Hall effect in a variety of magnetic insulating states at integer fillings of twisted MoTe2 moiré superlattice, including topologically trivial and nontrivial ferro-, antiferro-, and ferri-magnetic configurations. The dipole Hall current, in linear response to in-plane electric field, generates an in-plane orbital magnetization M∥ along the field, through which an AC field can drive magnetization oscillation up to THz range.

pmc-11700239.title: Electropolymerization of PPy, PEDOT, and PANi on WO3 nanostructures for high-performance anodes in Li-ion batteries
pmc-11700239.creator: Gemma Roselló-Márquez, Dionisio Miguel García-García, Mireia Cifre-Herrando, José García-Antón
pmc-11700239.description: In this research work, four distinct WO3 electrodes were synthesized and coated with three different polymers, known as polypyrrole (PPy), poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) in poly(4-styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) and polyaniline (PANi), using electropolymerization techniques. The morphological features of the samples were thoroughly characterized through Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FE-SEM) and Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) analyses.

pmc-13043071.title: Relationship Between Clostridioides difficile Stool Concentration, Nucleic Acid Amplification Test Results, and Environmental Contamination
pmc-13043071.creator: Mary Morgan Lee, Kimberly A Reske, Tiffany Hink, Skye R S Fishbein, Erin P Newcomer, Candice Cass, Margaret A Olsen, Gautam Dantas, Carey-Ann D Burnham, Erik R Dubberke
pmc-13043071.description: We compared rectal swab nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) with stool culture to detect Clostridioides difficile colonization and correlated results with environmental contamination. Rectal swab NAAT sensitivity (43%) for detecting toxigenic C. difficile colonization was low. Toxigenic culture-positive patients were more likely to have C. difficile detected in the hospital environment.

pmc-13091270.title: Evaluation of a facilitator training program in a randomized controlled trial of psilocybin treatment for depression
pmc-13091270.creator: Nikita Morel, Dea Siggaard Stenbaek, Johan Lundberg, Maria Beckman
pmc-13091270.description: BackgroundMajor depression is a prevalent condition among patients with life-threatening illnesses, such as cancer, and recent findings suggest that psilocybin may hold promising treatment potential. Contemporary trials of psilocybin generally employ a model that includes psychotherapeutic support consisting of preparation and integration sessions surrounding the dosing.

pmc-13353017.title: Effect of vitamin D deficiency on pregnancy outcomes in obese and non-obese pregnant women
pmc-13353017.creator: Omer Bardak, Oguzhan Gunenc, Emre Uysal, Sibel Ozler
pmc-13353017.description: BackgroundObesity and vitamin D deficiency are significant risk factors for adverse pregnancy outcomes. While lower vitamin D levels are common in obese individuals, their combined effect on perinatal outcomes remains controversial.ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the association between vitamin D deficiency and adverse perinatal outcomes in obese and non-obese pregnant women.

pmc-13674310.title: Identifying low-quality features and suboptimal models to enhance phenotype prediction
pmc-13674310.creator: Baining Shen, Min Li, Xiaoyue Hu, Ming Chen, Wei-Hua Chen, Hangjin Jiang
pmc-13674310.description: SummaryIt is common to build predictive models for complex phenotypes, such as diseases, where sample sizes are often limited by the cost of data collection. Machine learning and statistical methods are widely used in these cases. However, they may fail to identify high-quality features and lead to suboptimal models with high underfitting or overfitting risks.
